title: Arrhenius equation
examples: How does temperature affect the rate constant?
Can we use this graph to find the activation energy?
What is the relationship between the slope and Ea?

explain.say: Today we look at how temperature affects reaction rates. We use the Arrhenius equation for this.
The equation can be rearranged into a linear form. This helps us graph the data easily.
When we plot the natural log of k against the reciprocal of temperature, we get a straight line. The slope is important.
The slope of this line is equal to negative activation energy divided by the gas constant. This lets us find Ea.
If you know the slope from your graph, you can calculate the activation energy. Remember to use the correct units.
In a real chemical reaction, the rate constant changes with temperature. We plot these values to find Ea.

faq.q: What does the Arrhenius equation actually tell us?
faq.a: It describes how the rate constant of a reaction depends on temperature. It links the rate to the activation energy.
asks: How is temperature related to reaction rate?
Does this equation predict the rate change?

faq.q: Why do we plot ln k against 1 over T?
faq.a: Because the equation becomes linear in this form. Linear graphs are easy to analyze to find constants.
asks: Is there another way to graph this?

faq.q: What does the slope of the graph represent?
faq.a: The slope is equal to negative activation energy divided by the gas constant. This is crucial for finding Ea.
asks: What is the relationship between slope and Ea?
If the slope is positive, what does that mean?

faq.q: Is the activation energy the same as the enthalpy change?
faq.a: No, activation energy is the energy needed to start the reaction. Enthalpy change is the overall energy difference between reactants and products.
asks: What is the difference between the two energies?

faq.q: What are the units for the activation energy?
faq.a: The units for activation energy are the same as the energy units used for the gas constant, typically Joules per mole.
asks: What units should I expect for Ea?
Does R affect the units of Ea?

facts: The Arrhenius equation relates the rate constant to temperature.
Plotting ln k versus one over T yields a straight line.
The slope of this line is equal to negative activation energy divided by the gas constant.
Activation energy represents the minimum energy required for a reaction to occur.

quiz.say: If the slope of the ln k versus 1/T graph is negative, what must the activation energy be?
quiz.why: A negative slope multiplied by a negative sign gives a positive activation energy.

wrong.1: This would imply the reaction speeds up as temperature decreases.
wrong.2: This would mean the reaction rate is independent of temperature.
wrong.3: The slope only depends on Ea and R, not the pre-exponential factor A.

quiz.say: To find the activation energy, which values must you calculate from the graph?
quiz.why: The slope is the direct value read from the linear plot.

wrong.0: k changes at every point; we need the slope across all points.
wrong.2: The y-intercept gives ln A, not the activation energy.
wrong.3: The x-intercept relates to a specific temperature, not Ea.

quiz.say: If you double the temperature, what happens to the rate constant k?
quiz.why: The relationship is exponential, not linear, so the increase is large.

wrong.1: The relationship is much stronger than simple doubling.
wrong.2: Temperature is a major factor in reaction rates.
wrong.3: Higher temperatures always increase reaction rates.
